avis.titre: Good for Dry and Sensitive skin
avis.texte: [I received this product in exchange for my honest review] First aid beauty has always been my go to for the facial exfoliating pads and exfoliating products in general. I don't know 100% if these are new or just repackaged versions of the ones they previously had, but I really like how they don't sting when using. I have dry sensitive skin, especially on my face, so I hate using anything that makes my redness worse or stings when using. This did neither of those. It didn't not make my redness any worse and it didn't sting my face, it did really exfoliate the dead skin cells and help the other products I use after make my skin feel smooth and hydrated. I like that it has both lactic and gylcolic acids in here, and doesn't just say aha or bha, and tells you which acid, rather than having to look it up. This also works wonders on KP. I have it on my legs and the backs of my arms and other places, so when I get out of the shower, I often use a pad on those areas before moisturizer, to help tame it. Definitely recommend these if you have dry sensitive skin.

avis.titre: First Aid Beauty Brighten + Glow Facial Radiance Pads
avis.texte: These pads absorb quickly into the skin and don't leave any sticky residue, making them easy to use right after cleansing. The formula is lightweight, and the pad itself has a soft-textured feel — gentle enough for most skin types but still gives a light exfoliating sweep. In terms of effectiveness, they work gradually. With regular use, skin looks smoother, a bit brighter, and more even in tone. Results aren't dramatic overnight, but consistency makes a noticeable difference. The glow usually lasts throughout the day, especially when followed by moisturizer. Each jar comes with 60 pre-soaked pads, which is a good amount and lasts a while depending on how often you use them. Overall, they're a simple, gentle, and convenient way to maintain skin clarity and radiance.
